task.title: Nine files exceed the 250-line limit; most crossed it during this session

acceptance_criteria:
MEASURED 2026-11-06 with `miter audit --path . --threshold 250`: nine files exceed the hard limit, and most were pushed over during this session rather than being pre-existing. This is not the 200-250 band that GB-195 sweeps - these are violations of the limit itself.

  318  benchwork/crates/benchwork-core/src/migration/engine.rs
  313  chalkline/crates/chalkline-core/src/docs/decisions.rs      (created for GB-276)
  267  benchwork/crates/benchwork-core/src/telemetry_index.rs   (created for GB-243)
  265  storypole/crates/storypole-core/src/ledger/replay.rs      (edited for SP-27)
  265  benchwork/crates/benchwork-core/src/spec_studio.rs         (edited for GB-282)
  263  chalkline/crates/chalkline-cli/src/handlers_docs.rs
  258  storypole/crates/storypole-cli/src/handlers/lifecycle_cmds.rs
  254  storypole/crates/storypole-cli/src/handlers/core_cmds.rs
  253  outfeed/crates/outfeed-core/src/install/mod.rs

Why it went unnoticed: I ran `miter audit` per repository at the moment I touched it, and only for the crate I was changing. Several of these crossed the line in a commit whose repo-level audit I never ran, and the full-tree audit had not been run since before this session. The per-repo habit is not sufficient - the audit needs to run across the workspace as part of the completion gate, which is what Tier 3 claims to check.

Splitting strategy per file, to be applied together:
- decisions.rs: separate the MADR header parsing from the chronology enforcement, as the file already has two jobs.
- telemetry_index.rs: the sqlite projection is one job; the query surface is another.
- migration/engine.rs: split staging from apply, which is also what GB-267's reconciler work implies.
- replay.rs: event application versus state reconstruction.
- spec_studio.rs: bundle loading versus doc rewrite.
- the three storypole-cli handler files: one file per command family.

Not fixed inline here because it is nine files across five repositories and deserves its own atomic commits, not a tail-end edit to a question about layering.

DONE 2026-11-06. Nine files were over the hard 250-line limit; all nine are split and the full-tree audit now reports 'No files exceed 250 lines'.

Commits: 67e40fa (chalkline, 2 files), 65dfcae (benchwork, 3), dd13eb4 (storypole, 3), bb079c5 (outfeed, 1).

Splits, each at a seam that already existed in behaviour rather than at an arbitrary line count:
  decisions.rs 313 -> mod 141 + decision_finding 172      finding type and audit entry point vs MADR rules
  handlers_docs.rs 263 -> mod 133 + check 147             the Check arm was a module-sized match arm
  telemetry_index.rs 267 -> mod 212 + tests 61            the excess was tests, and the limit counts tests
  spec_studio.rs 265 -> mod 157 + decisions 117           reading a spec cannot corrupt it; editing can
  migration/engine.rs 318 -> mod 182 + reconcile 147      the boundary GB-267 already drew in behaviour
  replay.rs 265 -> mod 239 + cascade 27                   replay applies events; a cascade reaches backwards
  lifecycle_cmds.rs 258 -> mod 186 + decisions 73         lease conversation vs decision conversation
  core_cmds.rs 254 -> mod 136 + tasks 119                 changing a task's shape vs creating and querying
  install/mod.rs 253 -> mod 203 + staleness 62            staleness is answerable without knowing install

How they were missed, since the number matters: I ran `miter audit` per repository at the moment I touched it, and never across the tree. Several crossed the limit in commits where the repo-level audit ran a different repo or was skipped, so a green report meant only that the command I ran could not have caught it. That is the same shape as GB-287 - a check that cannot fail is not a check. The lesson is in the ticket: the audit belongs in the completion gate across the whole workspace, not as a per-repo habit.

Verification: per-repo Tier 2 on each touched repo (fmt, clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings, nextest) - chalkline 29, benchwork 59, storypole 64, outfeed 91 tests green. Workspace gates: miter contracts 0 drift, 11/11 lockfiles fresh, docs 108 present 0 drifted, layers clean at 1 lateral edge (dado-core -> miter-polyglot, blocked on MTR-22), downward 154.
